_comment: Editor layout for the kinetic reaction-scheme model (ReactionModel). Its predecessor ReactionWidget was abstract — no update_model — so it could never be opened and there is no before-image to compare against; functional compatibility with what its .ui offered is the bar. Deliberate difference: the fit range is NOT duplicated here. The old widget embedded a whole FittingControllerWidget in the model panel, which is the fit window's own control; only the autoscale toggle that reads that range is a model setting.

buttons.label: ➕ Add species
buttons.description: Append a species with zero starting concentration.

buttons.label: ➖ Remove
buttons.description: Drop the last species; two always remain, since a reaction needs a side each.

sections.description: Concentration at t=0 and brightness per species. The observed signal is the concentrations weighted by the brightnesses, so a dark intermediate is a species with Q = 0, not an absent one.

columns.label: Reaction
columns.description: The step, written with the species names.

columns.label: k
columns.description: Rate constant, in units of the data's time axis.

sections.description: Select a row to choose which reaction the Remove button drops.

buttons.label: ➕ Add step
buttons.description: Extend the chain by one unimolecular step into a new species.

buttons.label: ➖ Remove
buttons.description: Drop the selected reaction (the last one when nothing is selected).

buttons.label: ↺ Reset
buttons.description: Return to the default two-species A ⇌ B scheme.

sections.description: The rate constants, in reaction order — these are what the fit determines.

sections.label: Autoscale
sections.description: Rescale the model to the data's integral over the fit range instead of fitting the scaling factor. Useful while the scheme is still being set up.
Overall scaling, an additive background and a shift of the time axis (mixing dead time).

sections.title: Scheme (JSON)
sections.description: The whole scheme as text — paste one in to replace it, or copy it out to keep.
Reactions (educts, products, stoichiometries, rate) and species (name, concentration, brightness). Text that does not parse is ignored, so a half-typed scheme cannot destroy the current one.
